info.name: Omni-Platform API
info.description:
Covers every implemented feature: auth, channels, webhooks (with real HMAC/secret-token verification), contacts, conversations, flows, deals, campaigns, WhatsApp Tech Provider onboarding, templates, links/QR, search, and media.

SUGGESTED RUN ORDER: 1 Auth -> 2 Channels -> 3 Webhooks -> 4 Contacts -> 5 Conversations -> 6 Flows (then back to folder 2's 'Set Channel's Default Flow', then re-run folder 3 to see the flow engine react) -> 7 Deals -> 8 Campaigns -> 9/10 WhatsApp Onboarding + Templates (optional, needs real Meta credentials or a mock) -> 11 Links -> 12 Search -> 13 Media.

PREREQUISITES: the server running on {{baseUrl}} (default http://localhost:4000), Postgres + Redis at minimum. MongoDB is required for anything touching messages (folders 3, 5's message endpoints, 12). Elasticsearch is required for folder 12. Object storage (MinIO/S3) is required for folder 13. See IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md for which of these were live-tested during development vs. build-verified only.

Collection variables auto-populate as you run requests (token, tenantId, channelIds, flowId, etc.) — run folders roughly in order the first time through.

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Run Signup first — it creates a tenant + owner user and captures the JWT into {{token}} automatically for every other request in this collection.

request.description: Creates a new tenant + owner user. Change the email if you run this more than once — signup fails on a duplicate email.
Use this instead of Signup on subsequent test runs, once the account already exists.

item.name: 2. Channels
item.description: Creates channels directly (not via Embedded Signup) so the Webhooks folder has something to test against with a known, matching secret. See folder 9 for the real Tech Provider Embedded Signup flow.

request.description: credentials.appSecret matches {{whatsappAppSecret}} on purpose — the Webhooks folder signs its test payloads with the same value so signature verification passes.
Run this AFTER folder 6 (Flows) has published a flow and set {{flowId}}. Once set, the Webhooks folder's inbound messages will trigger the flow engine.

item.name: 3. Webhooks (simulate inbound messages)
item.description: Simulates Meta/Telegram delivering a real inbound message. This is what actually creates a contact + conversation + message — run this before folders 4/5 (Contacts/Conversations) or those will be empty. Requires MongoDB reachable (see IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md — message storage lives in Mongo, not Postgres).

request.description: Meta calls this once when you register a webhook URL. hub.verify_token must match WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN in your .env — the default there is 'change-me', matching this request.
Pre-request script computes a real HMAC-SHA256 signature over the exact body using {{whatsappAppSecret}} — must match the channel's credentials.appSecret from folder 2.

exec: // Postman's sandbox includes CryptoJS globally — no import needed.

item.name: 4. Contacts
item.description: Run folder 3 (Webhooks) first — contacts are created from inbound messages, not directly via the API.

request.description: Requires MongoDB reachable — messages are stored there, not Postgres.

item.name: 6. Flows
item.description: Create → publish a flow here, then go back to folder 2 to set it as the channel's default before re-running folder 3's webhooks to see it react.

item.name: 7. Deals
item.description: Run folder 3 (Webhooks) and folder 4 (Contacts) first so {{contactId}} is populated.

item.name: 8. Campaigns
item.description: Run folder 3+4 first so {{contactId}} is populated.

request.description: Sending will actually call the WhatsApp adapter's send() against the real (test) credentials — expect this to fail unless credentials.accessToken/phoneNumberId are real or apiBaseUrl is pointed at a mock. That failure is expected and fine for this test pass.
Drip steps send automatically via the scheduler in src/index.ts (see DRIP_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) — no manual 'send' call, unlike broadcasts.

item.name: 9. WhatsApp Onboarding (Tech Provider / Embedded Signup)
item.description: Optional — requires either real META_APP_ID/META_APP_SECRET configured against Meta, or META_GRAPH_API_BASE_URL pointed at a local mock (see IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md for how this was tested during development). The /callback request will fail against a default .env with no real Meta app configured — that's expected, not a bug.

item.name: 10. Templates
item.description: Requires a channel with a real wabaId — i.e. one onboarded via folder 9, not the manually-created channel from folder 2. Uses {{embeddedSignupChannelId}}.

request.description: credentials.businessPhoneNumber must be set on the channel for WhatsApp deep links to build — the channel created in folder 2 doesn't set it, so this may 400. Add businessPhoneNumber via the Patch Channel request first if you want to test this end to end.

item.name: 12. Search
item.description: Requires Elasticsearch reachable (see IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md — not live-tested during development, only build-verified). Run folder 3 first so there's something to find.

item.name: 13. Media
item.description: Requires object storage reachable (MinIO via docker-compose, or real S3) AND an object that actually exists at the given key — this collection has no way to create real WhatsApp/Telegram media via a mock, so this request is illustrative and will likely 404 unless you've received a real media message first.
